operations.value: Facet should become a full decision workspace with presentation quality that exceeds Lavish and review functionality that goes materially further. The goal is not decorative HTML volume: it is modular creative composition, excellent interaction design, durable collaboration, and substantially lower Codex usage. The product promise is: turn compact agent intent into a premium adaptive workspace, guide people from evidence to decision, then return precise feedback as tiny semantic changes.

node.title: Design reference — shadcn principles, Facet identity
node.text: Use shadcn/ui as a quality reference for composable accessible primitives, thoughtful defaults, calm neutral surfaces, disciplined spacing, clear component states, responsive sidebars, dialogs, sheets, tables, charts, and command interfaces. Do not clone its site or make shadcn a runtime requirement. Facet should translate those principles into dependency-light semantic renderer primitives and retain its own violet-and-cyan identity, review modes, local-first security boundary, and artifact protocol.

node.title: Color direction — neutral precision with expressive signals
node.text: Adopt a shadcn-inspired neutral foundation so content, evidence, and decisions carry the visual weight. Keep color purposeful: violet for primary action and active review state, cyan for keyboard focus and live location, and semantic colors for outcomes. These are proposed tokens and must pass automated and manual contrast checks before implementation.

rows: Primary actions, selected anchors, Decide mode
Outcome states reinforced by icon and text

node.title: Modular composition system
node.text: Build the UI as replaceable layers. Primitives guarantee accessibility and states; semantic blocks express review meaning; layout recipes compose blocks for a task; visual lenses let the user change perspective without regenerating content. Each layer remains deterministic and locally rendered so visual richness costs almost no additional model output.

data.summary: Design tokens feed accessible primitives, semantic blocks, adaptive recipes, and user-selectable review lenses

Semantic blocks — option, risk, evidence, recommendation, scorecard, timeline, diagram

node.title: Functionality beyond Lavish
node.text: Facet should pair premium composition with capabilities that improve the complete decision lifecycle. The differentiator is not the number of components; it is how evidence, discussion, change, and commitment remain connected.

node.title: Creative interaction ideas
node.text: Add a Decision Cockpit that condenses recommendation, unresolved risks, confidence, and next action into one focused surface. Introduce Evidence Gravity so strongly supported claims visually gain weight while uncertain assumptions remain visibly provisional. Offer Story mode for guided presentation, Board mode for spatial comparison, and Focus mode for deep reading from the same artifact. Add a Revision Radar that highlights semantic change by importance, a Devil's Advocate lens that foregrounds counterarguments already present in the artifact, and a Token Receipt that shows the cost of initial creation and each revision. These experiences must be derived from structured data—not generated decoration—and must remain readable without animation or color.

node.title: Visual acceptance pack for the proof sprint
node.text: The first implementation increment is complete only when one end-to-end review demonstrates the new design system and interaction depth across realistic states.

items: Desktop shell at 1440 and 1024 pixels with collapsible navigation and review rail
Tablet and mobile compositions at 768 and 375 pixels with a deliberate feedback sheet
Option Showdown recipe using modular comparison, risk, recommendation, and decision blocks
Explore, Review, and Decide states that are visually distinct without disabling comprehension
Empty, loading, saved, pending, failed, stale-anchor, conflict, offline, and resolved states
Light canvas and dark workspace themes with AA contrast and visible keyboard focus
Motion that explains selection and panel movement, with full reduced-motion behavior
Blind comparison against the Lavish reference using equal content and functionality

value: Stage 0 — Proof baseline: capture identical Facet and Lavish outputs, revisions, screenshots, timing, parity, and token estimates across five workflows.

Stage 1 — Design foundation: formalize the neutral-plus-violet token system and build accessible modular primitives inspired by shadcn's composability, without adding a mandatory framework dependency.
Stage 2 — Composition engine: ship executive brief, option showdown, and roadmap recipes plus summary bands, evidence clusters, scorecards, and premium decision controls.
Stage 3 — Review depth: add annotation pins, threads, guided review, evidence graph, change map, semantic before/after, decision rationale, and review lenses.
Stage 4 — Token compiler: shorten skill instructions, compile intent locally, apply defaults, validate automatically, and generate minimal patches, inbox digests, and token receipts.
Stage 5 — Creative expansion: add Story, Board, Focus, Decision Cockpit, Revision Radar, and only those semantic blocks validated by real workflows.
Stage 6 — Product proof: run blind visual-preference and task-completion studies, fix the largest failures, and claim superiority only after quality and efficiency gates pass.

operations.value: Use the shadcn reference as a compositional benchmark: quiet neutral foundations, crisp typography, deliberate borders, confident control states, and modular blocks. Facet must exceed it through task-aware composition and integrated review intelligence rather than ornamental effects.

Implement Facet sequentially through seven gated phases. Each phase must leave the repository buildable, preserve existing review behavior, and produce reviewable evidence. Estimates are working ranges for focused implementation, not calendar commitments. Publishing and hosted collaboration remain outside this plan until the local product passes Phase 6.

value: Phase 0 — Baseline and contracts (2–3 focused days): freeze competitive prompts, scoring rules, screenshots, current performance, token estimates, compatibility fixtures, and regression tests.

Phase 1 — Design foundation and shell (4–6 focused days): implement the neutral-plus-violet tokens, typography, spacing, accessible primitives, responsive application shell, navigation, review rail, command surface, and complete interaction states.

Phase 2 — Option Showdown vertical slice (5–7 focused days): build the adaptive recipe engine and redesign comparison, risk, recommendation, evidence, and decision blocks around one excellent end-to-end expense-tracker review.

Phase 3 — Review intelligence (6–8 focused days): add visible anchors, threaded feedback, review filters, guided progression, semantic change map, decision rationale, confidence, ownership, and supersession history.

Phase 4 — Token compiler and patch loop (5–7 focused days): compile compact intent locally, apply defaults and stable IDs, validate automatically, emit feedback digests, optimize patches, and display honest Token Receipts.

Phase 5 — Creative workspace modes (6–10 focused days): add Summary, Evidence, Risk, Change, Decision, Story, Board, and Focus lenses plus Decision Cockpit, Evidence Gravity, Revision Radar, and graceful legacy fallbacks.

Phase 6 — Competitive proof and release decision (7–10 focused days plus participant scheduling): run blind Facet-versus-Lavish comparisons, usability sessions, accessibility and performance audits, fix critical gaps, and decide whether a local alpha is ready.

node.title: Phase-by-phase delivery contract
node.text: Every phase has one dominant outcome and a measurable exit gate. Work that belongs to a later phase is recorded but not pulled forward unless it blocks the current gate.

node.title: Rules for phase-wise implementation
node.text: These rules keep quality high and make rollback straightforward while the renderer, protocol, and skill evolve together.

items: Create a scoped implementation brief and acceptance checklist before each phase begins.
Keep every commit buildable and preserve unrelated user changes.
Add tests with each new primitive, block, recipe, state, and protocol behavior.
Compare desktop, tablet, and mobile screenshots before closing visual work.
Run keyboard, screen-reader semantics, contrast, reduced-motion, offline, restart, and export checks at the relevant gate.
Record token, bundle, latency, and compatibility changes without overwriting earlier evidence.
Do not add a new semantic block when an existing block plus a layout recipe can express the same meaning.
Do not move to the next phase with unresolved critical or high-severity defects.
Review and approve the phase result in Facet before beginning the next phase.
Keep publishing, marketplace release, accounts, and hosted collaboration out of scope until separately approved.

operations.value: Begin with Phase 0, then proceed to Phase 1 only after the baseline evidence and contracts are frozen. The first visible milestone is the redesigned Option Showdown vertical slice in Phase 2; the foundation phases exist to make that result reusable rather than a one-off mockup.

value: Phase 0.1 — Freeze five identical competitor prompts and the equal-content, equal-function scoring rubric.
Phase 0.2 — Capture untouched current outputs, screenshots, timings, failures, retries, and token estimates.
Phase 0.3 — Record current build, test, accessibility, responsive, offline, export, and patch baselines.
Phase 0.4 — Freeze compatibility fixtures and define which existing behaviors cannot regress.
Phase 0 gate — Review the evidence pack and approve the exact Phase 1 scope.
Phase 1.1 — Implement tokens and primitive states without changing artifact semantics.
Phase 1.2 — Build the responsive shell, collapsible navigation, review rail, command surface, and mode indicators.
Phase 1 gate — Complete visual, responsive, accessibility, performance, and regression review before Phase 2.
